messages:
Ravi: Quick sync on auth surface after the RFC: propose defaulting to project-scoped API keys with a compact role_mask claim. Keeps check cheap on hot paths.
Nora: Means most services don't need a DB lookup for permission checks, right? Good. How do we handle admin tools that need org-level reach?
Ravi: Two options: (A) umbrella tokens that can mint ephemeral project tokens, OR (B) keep a small set of explicit org-admin tokens gated by MFA & audit. Leaning to umbrella flow for programmatic pipelines.
Lee: Umbrella sounds safer if minting is constrained. Must have strict mint quotas, short TTLs, and an audit_id in the claim.
Jules: Migration nag: infra still has long-lived org keys. We need a backward-compat shim so we don't break batch jobs during rollout.
Ravi: Plan: ingress transform that accepts old org-keys and issues equivalent project-scoped claims for a grace period. Shadow-emit audit lines and warn owners.
Nora: Request: make role_mask encoding deterministic and tiny (e.g., 16-bit hex). Add a mapping doc for role->bit.
Lee: For runtime, prefer decoding mask once per request header parsing stage and store as integer on the request context. No JSON role array.
Jules: Also document failure modes: expired umbrella, mint quota exceeded, and how clients observe errors. Add clear 403 vs 429 semantics.
AuthBot: RFC pointer: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/authn-compact-tokens-v1 (auto). Issue INF-4021 created to track shim rollout (auto).
